Other ma­te­rials, such as air or mixtures of salt and water, are classified as ­homogeneous materials because their properties are the same through- out a given sample. We cannot call these homogeneous materials pure substances, however. We still have to call them ­mixtures, because it is possible to separate them into components by ordinary physical means such as melting, freezing, boiling, or dissolving in solvents (Fig. 1.4).
